========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Yeah… I think maybe a little. I don’t know if I would have described it as my face being “flat” exactly, because I’m not watching myself from the outside, but I’ve noticed I don’t have the same kind of spark I usually do.

Like, I still get things done, but it’s in pieces. I’ll do the necessary part of a client thing, then leave the follow-up sitting there even when I know it matters. And it’s not always panic or anything dramatic — sometimes it’s just like I can’t find the push to care in the normal way. The email is right there, I know what I need to say, and I just… don’t.

Outside work, too, I’ve skipped jazz nights I normally like, and pickup basketball, and it doesn’t even bother me as much as it should. Before, if I missed those things, I’d feel like I was missing out or letting the week get away from me. Now it’s more like, “Okay, I’m not going,” and there’s not much feeling attached to it.

And with friends, when they ask what’s going on, I give these short answers. Not because I’m trying to be rude, exactly. It’s more like talking takes more effort than it should, even if the person matters to me. So… yeah, I guess my voice or expression might come across less animated. I haven’t had a lot of people tell me that directly, but from the inside it feels like there’s less there to show.

So… no, I don’t think I’ve been hearing voices.\n\nDoctor: Have there been times when your mood felt unusually high, energized, or irritable for days at a time?\n\nPatient: I’m not sure I’d say that, no. I mean, I have days where I’m more keyed up or irritated than usual, especially if I’m stressed or if something is bothering me and I can’t quite let it go, but I don’t think I’ve had stretches where I’m unusually high or energized for days in the way you might mean.\n\nI haven’t had, like, a period where I suddenly felt amazing and unstoppable or anything like that. And I don’t think I’ve been going for days with tons of extra energy. Irritable, maybe sometimes, but it feels more like normal frustration or tension than some big mood shift. So… I guess my answer is probably no, not really.\n\nDoctor: When you try to consider the possibility that these patterns are just coincidences, does that feel genuinely possible to you?\n\nPatient: I can say it to myself, like, “Maybe this is all coincidence,” and I do try to hold onto that for a minute. I’m not completely unwilling to consider it. But honestly, it doesn’t feel very believable once I start thinking through the specifics.\n\nBecause it isn’t just one thing. It’s not just, you know, one panel topic that happens to overlap with a conversation I had, or one person sitting near me at an event. It’s the way it repeats across these arts and finance circles here, where I’ll meet with a client or talk about something privately, and then suddenly an invitation comes through that seems to echo it, or the subject of a discussion lines up too closely, or someone connected to that world ends up near me in a way that feels arranged.\n\nSo, genuinely possible? Even when I try to talk myself down, I end up back at, “No, someone is tracking this somehow, or people are signaling something.” I don’t have the kind of proof where I could lay it out on a spreadsheet and convince someone else, but I also can’t really let it go.\n\nDoctor: Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?\n\nPatient: I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’ve felt weighed down at times, and I can get kind of stuck in my head, but I wouldn’t describe it as being depressed most of the day nearly every day.\n\nIt’s more like… certain days feel heavier than others, especially if I’ve been thinking a lot or feeling uncertain about things, but it’s not this constant low mood from morning to night. I still have stretches where I’m functioning and talking to people and doing what I need to do. Not years or anything like that. But over those two months it’s kept happening enough that it became harder for me to ignore. I mean, I do get caught on thoughts, and I’ll go over things in my head more than I probably should, but “repetitive unwanted thoughts” makes me think of something more like a phrase or image that keeps forcing itself in, and I don’t know that that’s what I’m experiencing.\n\nThe part about recognizing them as coming from my own mind is also… I don’t know. So I wouldn’t want to say yes if you mean thoughts that I clearly know are just internal and irrational but can’t resist. Like even explaining myself feels tiring. So yes, I guess I have lost some interest, or at least I’m not connecting with people and activities the way I used to.\n\nDoctor: Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from topic to topic in a way that doesn’t make sense to them?\n\nPatient: I don’t think anyone has said it to me that directly, no. Like, no one has pulled me aside and said, “You’re not making sense,” or “You’re jumping all over the place.” At least not in those words.\n\nSometimes I’ll notice people pause or ask me to repeat what I mean, especially if I’m trying to explain something with a lot of moving parts, but I’ve always been kind of detailed when I talk. In my work, I’m used to giving background and context, because if you leave out one piece, the whole thing can sound different. So I might circle around a point more than some people would like, but I don’t know that it’s been hard to follow in a strange way.\n\nI guess my answer is… not really, or not that I’ve noticed. If people think that, they haven’t told me clearly.\n\nDoctor: During this two-month period, has this sense that people are tracking you been present on most days?\n\nPatient: Yeah… most days, I’d say. It hasn’t been every single minute or anything, but the sense of it has been around pretty consistently.\n\nIt’s been about two months now that I’ve had this feeling that people are tracking my client meetings, or at least paying attention to them in some organized way. Some days it’s stronger than others, but it hasn’t really gone away for more than maybe a short stretch. So if you mean during that two-month period, was it there on most days, then… yes, I think that’s fair to say.\n\nDoctor: Since this started, has your ability to function at work or in daily life clearly gotten worse?\n\nPatient: Yeah… I think it has, but not in a dramatic way like I stopped showing up or anything. Like normally, after a meeting, I’d send the summary, check in about paperwork, schedule the next conversation, keep that relationship warm. And lately those things are slipping. Not always, but enough that I can see the difference.\n\nI’ve also been avoiding some public-facing stuff, like panels or events where I’d normally talk to potential clients or be visible. I used to do those because they helped bring people in, and I was comfortable enough with it. Now I find reasons not to go, or I’ll tell myself it’s not worth the time, but I think it’s more than that.\n\nSo daily life… I mean, I’m functioning. I pay bills, I get dressed, I go to work. No… I don’t think it’s like my body is being controlled, if that’s what you mean. I don’t feel like someone is moving my arms or making me walk somewhere against my will.

What brought me in is more… it’s more about feeling like certain people are tracking me, or tracking who I meet with. So no, I wouldn’t say outside forces are controlling my actions. It’s more like I feel watched, or followed indirectly, and like there are messages being sent through normal things.

So… yes, roughly two months that I’ve had that feeling people may be tracking what I’m doing or sending me messages in some indirect way.\n\nDoctor: Do you have repetitive unwanted thoughts that you recognize as coming from your own mind and that feel intrusive or hard to resist?\n\nPatient: I’m not sure I’d describe it that way, exactly. But I don’t experience it as, like, an unwanted mental tic or something I can simply label as “just my mind” and push away.\n\nDoctor: Have you found yourself losing interest in people or activities you used to care about?\n\nPatient: Yeah… I think so, at least somewhat. So yes, I guess I have lost some interest, or at least I’m not connecting with people and activities the way I used to.\n\nDoctor: Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from topic to topic in a way that doesn’t make sense to them?\n\nPatient: I don’t think anyone has said it to me that directly, no. In my work, I’m used to giving background and context, because if you leave out one piece, the whole thing can sound different. Not impossible exactly… I mean, not like the TV is speaking to me personally, or the radio is sending coded messages with my name in them. I don’t really watch something and think the anchor is talking directly to me, if that’s what you mean.

I know those are normal things, technically. Invitations and panels and people sitting places are not supernatural. But the pattern feels too specific to ignore. I can tell myself, “Maybe this is coincidence, maybe you’re making connections that aren’t there,” but then another thing happens and I can’t really let it go. So… no, not impossible through television or radio, but yes, I do feel like messages are being sent to me through normal events and communications.
